clues.title: Plate: large white, yellow for commercial
text: Thailand uses large, **white** licence plates on **passenger vehicles**, and yellow ones on commercial vehicles.
NOTE: Within Southeast Asia, yellow commercial plates are only found in Thailand. Be careful, however, as Laos uses yellow licence plates for regular vehicles.

images.caption: Thai plates: standard white and yellow commercial

clues.summary: Big white plates on private vehicles, yellow on commercial ones. Yellow commercial plates are only found here in Southeast Asia, but Laos uses yellow on normal cars.

differs.how: Laos uses short yellow plates on ordinary cars

clues.title: Driving side: left
text: Thailand drives on the **left hand** side of the road.
NOTE: Cambodia, Vietnam and Laos drive on the right hand side.
clues.summary: Traffic drives on the left. Cambodia, Vietnam and Laos drive on the right.

clues.title: Bollard: square, pointed top, striped
text: The Thai bollard is square shaped with a pointed top, and has **black-and-white stripes**.
NOTE: In Southeast Asia, these bollards are also found in Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia.
clues.summary: Square concrete bollard with a pointed top and black-and-white stripes. Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia have it too.

clues.title: Sign: bulky white signpost, black bottom
text: Signposts in Thailand are square and bulky in shape, usually white, and often have the **bottom painted black**.
NOTE: In Southeast Asia, this design is unique to Thailand.
clues.summary: Square, bulky, usually white signposts, often with the bottom painted black. Unique in Southeast Asia.

clues.title: Road: concrete with big square slabs
text: **Concrete roads** are common in Thailand. They often have a large square shaped pattern.
NOTE: In Southeast Asia, these can also be found commonly in the Philippines, and less commonly in Indonesia.

images.caption: A concrete road made of big square slabs

clues.summary: Concrete roads with a large square pattern are common. The Philippines has them too, Indonesia less often.

clues.title: Pole: square with holes up the side
text: Thai poles are **square **and have small **holes** running vertically up the pole.
NOTE: You will see similar poles in Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Laos. Make sure to look for other clues before guessing.
clues.summary: Square concrete poles with small vertical holes. Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Laos have similar ones, so check other clues.

clues.title: Language: compact script with tiny circles
text: **Thai script** is compact and in many fonts has tiny circles within most letters.

NOTE: The Cambodian (Khmer) script often has longer lines and more accents underneath the lettering, as opposed to the Thai script. The Lao script looks similar to the Thai script. Make sure to check the driving side before guessing.
clues.summary: Compact script with small circles in many letters. Cambodian script has longer lines and more marks underneath. Lao looks similar, so check the driving side.

differs.how: Cambodian script has longer lines, more marks below
Laos looks similar but drives on the right

clues.title: Road lines: yellow middle lines
text: Thailand has** yellow middle lines**. These middle lines are either solid or [dashed](https://goo.gl/maps/3skrWJJNZ7JxFzyi7) lines.
NOTE: Malaysia only has white middle lines.
clues.summary: Yellow middle lines, solid or dashed. Malaysia only has white middle lines.

differs.how: Malaysia only has white middle lines

clues.title: Pole: red-black or black-white striped base
text: Street light poles have **red-and-black** or **black-and-white** stripes on the bottom.
clues.summary: Street light poles have red-and-black or black-and-white stripes at the bottom.

clues.title: Poles: long thin lamp arms over the road
text: Thailand has very distinct long, thin **lamp posts** that hang over the side of the road.

images.caption: A long thin lamp arm reaching over the road

clues.summary: Very long, thin lamp posts that hang out over the side of the road.

clues.title: Sign: white two-part signs, green on highways
text: Directional signs on smaller roads are **white**, and are composed of two signs: one with an arrow at the bottom, and one with the information at the top. These can have place names. When they do not, you will see them as just the road number with a [Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emblem_of_Thailand). Moreover, highway signs are **green**, and frequently feature the place names in Latin script below the Thai name.
clues.summary: On smaller roads the signs are white, in two parts: an arrow below and info above. Without place names they just show the road number and a Garuda emblem. Highway signs are green, with Latin place names below the local ones.

clues.title: Sign: stop sign in local script, 3 characters
text: Stop signs in Thailand feature the **Thai script**, instead of Latin.
NOTE: Stop signs in Laos feature the Lao script, similar to Thai, but they have just 2 characters instead of 3.
clues.summary: Stop signs use Thai script, not Latin. Laos uses a similar script but has only 2 characters.

differs.how: Lao stop signs have 2 characters, not 3

clues.title: Marker: road markers with white or black Garuda
text: These two road markers are generally found in Thailand. They will either have a white or a black **Garuda** on them.

NOTE: White Garudas are found on national roads and appear [white](/images/thailand/Thai+roads.png) on the map, while black ones are found on provincial roads and appear [dark blue](/images/thailand/Thai+roads.png) on the map.

images.caption: Road markers with white or black tops: two examples

clues.summary: Road markers carry a white or black Garuda bird emblem. White is on national roads, black on provincial roads.

clues.title: Flags: many along the street, yellow royal
text: Thailand often has many flags lining the side of its streets. Aside from the national flag, you can often see [royal flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_flags_of_Thailand), which are usually **yellow**.

images.caption: A national flag and a yellow royal flag hanging along the street

clues.summary: Streets are often lined with flags: the national flag and yellow royal flags.

clues.title: Sign: distinctive green village sign
text: These distinctive **green **signs can be found all around Thailand, often in small villages.
NOTE: You will not find this sign in any other country.
clues.summary: A distinctive green sign found across the country, often in small villages. It exists in no other country.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 with no visible car
text: Most Generation 3 coverage has **no visible Street View car**.

NOTE: [Vientiane](https://maps.app.goo.gl/E53R9yBhmgzxiKaY8) and some Generation 3 coverage in [Cambodia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/G3n69goD22xopDMg7) will also not have a visible car. [Bike trekkers](https://maps.app.goo.gl/89XmAqRyVAqEU8wK6) and a [white car with a brake light](https://maps.app.goo.gl/SnHxSHmoqq64yXfr6) can rarely be found all throughout the country in Generation 3.
clues.summary: Most Gen 3 coverage shows no car. The Laos capital and some Gen 3 in Cambodia also have no car. Rare bike trekkers and a white car with a brake light appear too.

clues.title: Phone numbers: 9-digit landline, 02 for capital
text: Thai **landline phone numbers** have 9 digits. The first digits of phone numbers are the area code. The Bangkok area code is 02, the other area codes have three digits. The area codes are grouped, so even just learning the first digit is useful.
NOTE: Mobile phone numbers start with 08 or 09 and have 10 digits. None of these numbers overlap with the area codes. Numbers starting with 06 are also not regional.
clues.summary: Landlines have 9 digits. The capital's area code is 02 and others have three digits. Area codes are grouped, so the first digit helps. Mobiles start with 08 or 09 and have 10 digits, and 06 numbers are not regional.

clues.title: Route numbers: first digit shows region
text: National roads are grouped into four regions based on their **first digit**. Roads beginning with 1 can be found in the north, 2 in the northeast, 3 in the centre and 4 in the south of the country.
NOTE: Large one- and two-digit highways may pass through multiple regions. Remember that this map does not apply to provincial roads.
clues.summary: National roads starting with 1 are in the north, 2 the north-east, 3 the centre and 4 the south. Big one- and two-digit highways cross regions, and provincial roads don't follow this.

clues.title: Sign: two-letter province code on waystones
text: Waystones and road signs on provincial roads will often provide a **two-letter abbreviation** of the province in Thai script. They will not appear on waystones or road signs for national roads.
You can use [this](https://super-duper.fr/country/thailand_provinces_en.php) site to view and practice all province abbreviations.

images.caption: Red circle marks the two-letter Thai province code on the white concrete km marker

clues.summary: Waystones and road signs on provincial roads often show a two-letter province abbreviation in Thai script. National roads don't.

clues.title: Boxes: black boxes with 3-letter province code
text: These **black boxes** will often provide a **three-letter abbreviation** of the province. Two formats are used:
- Starting with the abbreviation followed by 4 numbers
- Starting with TCC-L2, or rarely TCC-L1, followed by the abbreviation
Shown in the picture is the abbreviation “NTB” for Nonthaburi. The abbreviations may vary slightly in each province depending on the format.
NOTE: Other boxes may feature different formats that correspond to the subdistrict of the province.

images.caption: Black boxes on a pole with a 3-letter province code

clues.summary: Black boxes often show a three-letter province code, either starting with it followed by 4 numbers, or starting with TCC-L2 followed by the code. Other boxes may show the subdistrict.

clues.title: Religion: Islamic dress and Jawi script
text: The majority of **Muslims** in Thailand live in the very south of the country. In these areas, you will often see Islamic religious attire, [Jawi script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawi_script), based on the Arabic script, on [signs](https://maps.app.goo.gl/oy83kvBm8XWcc3ZEA) and mosques.
clues.summary: Most Muslims live in the very south. There you often see Islamic dress, mosques and Jawi script, based on Arabic, on signs.

clues.title: Landscape: two flat, dry regions
text: Thailand has two regions that are relatively **flat and dry** compared to other areas. One north of Bangkok, the other more east.
NOTE: The eastern area feels sometimes a bit **drier** than the area north of Bangkok.
clues.summary: Two relatively flat and dry regions: one north of the capital, one further east. The eastern one can feel drier.

clues.title: Landscape: tall mountains in the north-west
text: **Tall mountains** are most often seen in northwestern** **Thailand.
NOTE: Some parts of the southern peninsular part are also mountainous.
clues.summary: Tall mountains are most often seen in the north-west, and also parts of the southern peninsula.

clues.title: Landscape: low smooth forested mountains
text: Low, smooth and forested mountains can be found in the centre-north of the country.
clues.summary: Low, smooth, forested mountains in the centre-north of the country.

clues.title: Landscape: steep rocky mountains, west and south
text: Steep mountains with a lot of **exposed rock** are most commonly found in the west and on the peninsula.
clues.summary: Steep mountains with a lot of bare rock, most common in the west and on the peninsula.

clues.title: Soil: red, mostly north-east
text: **Red soil** is most common in the northeast of Thailand, but can be seen throughout the entire country.
clues.summary: Red soil is most common in the north-east, but appears across the whole country.

clues.title: Roads: gravel roads
text: **Gravel roads** can be found all throughout Thailand, but are most common in the darkly highlighted areas.

images.caption: A gravel road between rice fields

clues.summary: Gravel roads appear everywhere but are most common in the darkly highlighted areas on the map.

clues.title: Plants: rubber trees with small black cups
text: **Rubber wood plantations** are typically seen in Thailand. Most of them are located in the** **south. You can recognize them by the small, black taps on the bottom of the tree's trunk.
clues.summary: Rubber plantations, mostly in the south. Look for small black cups at the bottom of the trunks.

clues.title: Farming: rice within highlighted area
text: A majority of Thailand’s **rice **cultivation occurs within the highlighted area.
clues.summary: Most rice is grown within the highlighted area on the map.

clues.title: Farming: dry-season rice in the central plains
text: **Rice** cultivated during the **dry season** is most common in the central plains. The dry season in Thailand can typically be recognized by a haze in the sky due to wildfires.
clues.summary: Dry-season rice is most common in the central plains. The dry season often shows as haze in the sky from wildfires.

clues.title: Farming: wet-season rice in the east
text: During the **wet season**, the majority of **rice **cultivation occurs in the eastern plains.
clues.summary: During the wet season, most rice is grown in the eastern plains.

clues.title: Plants: palm oil plantations, south
text: Over 90% of the palm oil in Thailand is produced in the south. This means that **palm plantations** are most often seen in southern Thailand.
clues.summary: Over 90% of palm oil is produced in the south, so oil palm plantations show up most there.

clues.title: Plants: dense short coconut groves
text: Dense plantations of** short **or **medium sized coconut palms** are most commonly found west** **of Bangkok.
clues.summary: Dense plantations of short or medium coconut palms, mostly west of the capital.

clues.title: Plants: tall coconut plantations, south-west
text: Slightly less dense plantations of **tall coconut palms **are most common in Prachuap Khiri Khan.
NOTE: The entire peninsula will have many coconut palms, this tip only refers to plantations.
clues.summary: Slightly less dense plantations of tall coconut palms, most common in one south-western province. The entire peninsula has many coconut palms, this is about plantations only.

clues.title: Plants: palmyra palms near the south-east coast
text: Large numbers of **palmyra palms** are typically found near the eastern coast of the peninsula, specifically just south of Bangkok as well as in the far south.
NOTE: Lone or small clusters of palmyra palms can be found all throughout the country.
clues.summary: Large numbers of palmyra palms near the eastern coast of the peninsula, just south of the capital and in the far south. Single or small groups appear everywhere.

clues.title: Plants: areca palms on the peninsula
text: **Areca palms** are mainly found across the peninsula, but are especially common around Ranong.
clues.summary: Areca palms are mainly on the peninsula, especially around one south-western town.

clues.title: Farming: sugar cane in the centre and east
text: **Sugar cane **is mostly grown in central and eastern Thailand.
clues.summary: Sugar cane is mostly grown in the centre and east.

clues.title: Plants: cassava, bush with fingered leaves
text: [**Cassava**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassava)** **is a bush-like plant with [digitate leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_leaf_morphology#/media/File:Leaf_morphology.svg). It** **can be found throughout most of Thailand, but is considerably more common in the central and northeastern plains.
clues.summary: Cassava is a bush with leaves split like fingers. Found in most of the country, but much more common in the central and north-eastern plains.

clues.title: Farming: corn in the north and centre
text: **Corn **is most commonly found in the north and central** **regions of Thailand.
clues.summary: Corn is most commonly seen in the north and central regions.

clues.title: Farming: big fruit plantations
text: The most extensive **fruit plantations** can be found in the valley between Chiang Mai and Lamphun** **as well as eastern Sa Kaeo and Chanthaburi.
clues.summary: The biggest fruit plantations are in a northern valley and in the far eastern provinces.

clues.title: Plants: durian plantations, cone-shaped young
text: **Durian plantations** are most common around Chanthaburi, but can be found around the peninsula and other areas. When they are young, they can be identified by their cone-shaped appearance. When [fully grown](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3TtjWxAX8eC8m72f7), durian trees can be identified by their dark bark, branches that nearly reach the ground, and oblong leaves with pointed tips.
clues.summary: Most common in the south-east but found on the peninsula and elsewhere. Young trees look cone-shaped. Grown ones have dark bark, branches nearly reaching the ground and pointed oblong leaves.

clues.title: Farming: pineapple plantations near the capital
text: **Pineapple plantations **are most commonly found southeast and southwest** **of Bangkok.
clues.summary: Pineapple plantations are most common south-east and south-west of the capital.

clues.title: Plants: eucalyptus plantations in the east
text: **Eucalyptus plantations** are most common around Sa Kaeo.
NOTE: Eucalyptus can be found in smaller quantities, such as lining the road, in different areas. This tip is exclusively about dense plantations.
clues.summary: Dense eucalyptus plantations are most common around one eastern border province. Eucalyptus lining roads can appear elsewhere in small amounts.

clues.title: Plants: teak, big leaves and yellow flowers
text: [Tectona grandis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teak), also known as **teak**, is most commonly found in high densities in the north. It can be recognized by its large leaves and yellow flowers.
NOTE: Teak trees are often used for decoration along [highways](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8ZVapgFjkxUqz6UB8).
clues.summary: Teak grows in high densities in the north. It has large leaves and yellow flowers, and is often planted as decoration along highways.

clues.title: Plants: Tenasserim pines in the north
text: **Pine trees**, specifically [Pinus latteri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_latteri), or Tenasserim pines, are more or less exclusive to the north and northwest of the country.
clues.summary: Pine trees of this kind are almost exclusively in the north and north-west.

clues.title: Plants: garden croton, yellow-red leaves
text: [Codiaeum variegatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codiaeum_variegatum), also known as **garden croton**, is a decorative plant recognised by its yellow, orange and red leaves. It is most common around Ranong and other coastal provinces.
clues.summary: A decorative plant with yellow, orange and red leaves, most common around one south-western town and other coastal provinces.

clues.title: Houses: grey corrugated metal roofs
text: **Gray corrugated metal roofs** are most commonly found in the north and south** **of the country, but can occasionally be found throughout the country.
clues.summary: Grey corrugated metal roofs are most common in the north and south, but appear everywhere occasionally.

clues.title: Pole: indented concrete near the capital
text: Regular poles with a Chilean style **indent **are found around Bangkok.
NOTE: Larger and thicker poles with indents are found on [highways](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8tzw2wz1WYcVC83R8) all throughout the country.

images.caption: Pole beside a pond; the red circle zooms in on an indented concrete pole, left

clues.summary: Regular poles with a Chile-style indent around the capital. Larger, thicker indented poles appear on highways everywhere.

clues.title: Landscape: wind turbines in a few places
text: **Wind turbines** are most often found on the western side of Chaiyaphum and Nakhon Ratchasima as well as the eastern coast of Songkhla and Nakhon Si Thammarat.
clues.summary: Wind turbines are mostly on the west side of two north-eastern provinces and on the eastern coast of two southern provinces.

clues.title: Bollard: black with three big white reflectors
text: This **black bollard** with **three large white reflectors** is most frequently seen in Chiang Mai and Mae Hong Son.
clues.summary: A black bollard with three large white reflectors, seen mostly in two north-western provinces.

clues.title: Pole: insulators with 7+ ridges
text: Insulators with **7 or more ridges** are found in the southern half of the peninsula, as well as highways in Chiang Rai and Phayao.
NOTE: In the north, you may still find 5 or 6 ridges on insulators, as these are the standard amount throughout the country.
clues.summary: Insulators with seven or more ridges are in the southern half of the peninsula and on highways in two northern provinces. Five or six ridges are standard everywhere else.

clues.title: Pole: single insulator on the crossbar
text: Poles with only **one insulator **on the crossbar can be found from south on the peninsula to Ranong and Chumphon.
clues.summary: Poles with just one insulator on the crossbar run from the southern peninsula up to two south-western provinces.

clues.title: Pole: two insulators on the crossbar
text: Conversely, poles with **two insulators** on the crossbar can be found in the rest of the country.
clues.summary: Poles with two insulators on the crossbar are found in the rest of the country.

clues.title: Landscape: touristy rich island with resorts
text: The island of **Phuket **is very touristy and wealthy. You will often see modern buildings, resorts, and heavy traffic among hills.
clues.summary: A wealthy tourist island with modern buildings, resorts and heavy traffic among hills.

clues.title: Landscape: touristy islands, narrow roads
text: Koh Samui and Koh Pha-Ngan are touristy islands with **narrow, crowded roads** and a tropical feel.

images.caption: A narrow road in a touristy island town

clues.summary: Two touristy islands with narrow, crowded roads and a tropical feel.

clues.title: Taxis: pink, or yellow on green
text: Bangkok uses **pink **and **yellow on green taxis**.
NOTE: Yellow on green taxis may rarely be seen [elsewhere](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Jf25hEoRKt9tQhvEA), but pink taxis are practically exclusive.

images.caption: Pink taxi and a yellow-on-green taxi

clues.summary: The capital has pink taxis and yellow-on-green ones. Yellow-on-green may rarely appear elsewhere, but pink is practically exclusive.

clues.title: Vehicles: red pickup-truck buses
text: These red trucks, known as **songthaews**, are transport vehicles found most commonly in Chiang Mai.
clues.summary: Red trucks called songthaews act as transport, most common in one northern city.

clues.title: Street sign: small green strip under blue
text: Street signs with a **smaller** **green section** underneath a blue section are found in Bangkok and Nonthaburi.
clues.summary: Street signs with a smaller green section beneath a blue section, found in the capital and a neighbouring province.

clues.title: Street sign: helmet-shaped
text: Street signs shaped like a **helm **are exclusive to Pattaya City.
clues.summary: Helmet-shaped street signs are found only in one seaside city.

clues.title: Street sign: red with golden border
text: **Red street signs** with golden decorated borders can be found in Mueang Chiang Rai.
NOTE: It is possible to see blue street signs with the same border in the city.
clues.summary: Red street signs with golden decorated borders are in one northern city. Blue ones with the same border also exist there.

clues.title: Landscape: flat valley ringed by mountains
text: The **Phrao District** in Chiang Mai is a fairly flat valley surrounded by mountains in all directions. The valley will commonly grow rice and fruit.
clues.summary: A fairly flat valley surrounded by mountains on every side, commonly growing rice and fruit.

clues.title: Landscape: third tallest mountain in view
text: **Doi Luang Chiang Dao** is the 3rd tallest mountain in Thailand. It along with other distinctly shaped mountains can be seen clearly from the Chiang Dao district of Chiang Mai.
clues.summary: The country's third tallest mountain and other distinctly shaped mountains can be seen clearly from one northern district.

clues.title: Landscape: jagged north-south ridge to the east
text: A large and slightly jagged north-south mountain ridge runs through the middle of **Phayao**. It can be seen to the east from afar.
clues.summary: A large, slightly jagged north-south ridge runs through the middle of one northern province, visible to the east from afar.

clues.title: Landscape: rolling hills of corn and sugar cane
text: **Rolling hills** of corn or sugar cane fields can be found in the west of the Tak province. In this area, paved roads are often [very brown](https://maps.app.goo.gl/gFH71bddWWbfX9Pz5).
clues.summary: Rolling hills of corn or sugar cane in the west of one province, where paved roads often look very brown.

clues.title: Landscape: big north-south mountains both sides
text: **Large north-south mountains** can be seen on either side of the Phetchabun valley.
clues.summary: Large north-south mountains on either side of a valley in the north-centre.

clues.title: Soil: deep red fields, cassava and rubber
text: **Deep red fields** with cassava and rubber trees can be found in Kanchanaburi.
clues.summary: Deep red fields with cassava and rubber trees in one western province.

clues.title: Landscape: distinctly shaped mountains, centre
text: These distinctly shaped mountains can be found in **southwestern Lopburi**.
clues.summary: Distinctly shaped mountains in the south-west of one central province.

clues.title: Landscape: big bare-rock mountains, east-west
text: The northern half of Saraburi consists of** large, exposed rock mountains** in an east-west orientation.
clues.summary: The northern half of one central province has large, exposed-rock mountains in an east-west line.

clues.title: Landscape: very long flat mountain ridges
text: Chaiyaphum features **very long and flat mountain ridges** that can be seen from nearly anywhere in the province.
clues.summary: Very long, flat mountain ridges visible from almost anywhere in one north-eastern province.

clues.title: Landscape: tourist road with resorts, rocky hills
text: The area around Khao Yai National Park in southern Nakhon Ratchasima is a **large tourist attraction**. You will see many advertisements, businesses, restaurants, and resorts along otherwise rural roads. Large rocky hills can be seen closer to the border with Nakhon Nayok and Prachin Buri.
clues.summary: Near a famous national park, rural roads are lined with ads, restaurants and resorts. Large rocky hills show closer to two neighbouring provinces.

clues.title: Landscape: jagged limestone peaks, far bank
text: In northern Nakhon Phanom, along the Mekong River, you will sometimes see **jagged limestone karst mountains** to the northeast. These formations stand on the Lao side and are often visible from long distances.
clues.summary: In the north-east along the Mekong you sometimes see jagged limestone peaks to the north-east. They stand on the Lao side and are visible from far away.

differs.how: The peaks themselves are in Laos

clues.title: Landscape: long low hills among crop fields
text: The province of Mukdahan features many **long, low hills** among fields of rice, sugarcane, cassava and rubber trees.
clues.summary: One north-eastern province has many long, low hills among fields of rice, sugarcane, cassava and rubber trees.

clues.title: Landscape: big bare-rock massifs
text: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park in western Prachuap Khiri Khan features large, distinct exposed rock mountain massifs. Notably, the mountains can be seen from the [center of the province](https://maps.app.goo.gl/SNn2WAdVCjAdX8mf9).
clues.summary: Large, distinct exposed-rock mountain massifs in a western coastal province, visible from the centre of the province.

clues.title: Landscape: tallest steep bare-rock mountains
text: Khao Sok National Park in northern Phang-nga and western Surat Thani features some of the **tallest and steepest exposed rock mountains** in the south of Thailand. The mountains generally run east-west.
clues.summary: Some of the tallest, steepest exposed-rock mountains in the south, running east-west, in a national park.

clues.title: Landscape: large bare-rock mountains, north-south
text: Western Krabi and parts of eastern Phang-nga also feature **large exposed rock mountains** running north-south.
clues.summary: Western Krabi and parts of eastern Phang-nga have large exposed-rock mountains running north-south.

clues.title: Road: brown paved road among sugarcane and corn
text: **Brown paved roads** among fields of sugarcane, cassava, and corn can be found in southeastern Nakhon Ratchasima.

images.caption: A brown paved road among sugarcane

clues.summary: Brown paved roads among sugarcane, cassava and corn fields, found in the south-east of one north-eastern province.

clues.title: Road: brown paved road among bananas and durians
text: **Brown paved roads** among fields of bananas, durians, rubber, and corn can be found in southern Sisaket.
NOTE: Southeastern Nakhon Ratchasima may look [similar](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3px9g5rxuA6NbzzL8) at times.

images.caption: A brown paved road among bananas

clues.summary: Brown paved roads among bananas, durians, rubber and corn, in the south of one north-eastern province. Another province may look similar.

clues.title: Fields: north-north-west grid, ridges around
text: Southern Lopburi features a large, slightly** north-north-west grid** with fields of rice, corn, sugarcane, and cassava. Ridges can often be seen to the north, south and west.
clues.summary: A large, slightly north-north-west grid of rice, corn, sugarcane and cassava fields, with ridges often visible to the north, south and west.

clues.title: Fields: large almost perfect north-south grid
text: A large, almost perfectly **north-south** **grid** can be found in central and eastern Pathum Thani.

images.caption: A concrete road beside large fields

clues.summary: A large, almost perfectly north-south grid in central and eastern parts of one central province.

clues.title: Fields: north-east to south-west grid, industry
text: Western Rayong province features a **northeast-southwest grid** filled with modern and industrial buildings among fields of rubber trees, cassava, and pineapple.
clues.summary: A north-east to south-west grid with modern and industrial buildings among rubber, cassava and pineapple fields, in the west of one eastern province.

clues.title: Road: four-lane divided with huge gap
text: Highway 44 going through Krabi and Surat Thani is a **divided four-lane highway** with **very large spacing** in the middle. Often, you will not be able to see the other side of the highway. Rather, a yellow inner line will imply that the road is divided.

images.caption: A four-lane divided road with a huge gap between the carriageways

clues.summary: A divided four-lane highway with a very wide gap in the middle. You often can't see the other side, but a yellow inner line shows the road is divided.

clues.title: Google car: rare car with a visible mirror
text: This rare Google car with a **visible mirror** is only found in far southern Thailand.
NOTE: Due to most of the coverage being overwritten by new Generation 4, this car is rarely seen.

clues.title: Google car: bars poking out of the blur

clues.summary: A rare Google car found only on one small island, recognisable by bars sticking out of the blur.

clues.title: Google car: smudge on front left of camera
text: A **smudge **on the** front left **of the camera can be seen on the densely forested road going through Khao Yai National Park. This smudge can also be found in nearby areas of Nakhon Nayok and Prachin Buri.
NOTE: Other smudges may rarely exist [elsewhere](https://maps.app.goo.gl/GYwj41y21n9awFLT6) in the country.

images.caption: Google car: a smudge on the front left of the camera, circled in red

clues.summary: A smudge on the front left of the camera appears on a densely forested national park road and in nearby provinces. Other smudges may rarely exist elsewhere.
